Adamaszek's Conjecture 7.4 on necklace cycle lengths

M. Adamaszek, Hard squares on cylinders revisited, arXiv:1202.1655v2, Section 7, Conjecture 7.4, states:

The length of every cycle in the graph Neck(k, n) divides n−3k. In other words, for every (k, n)-necklace N we have Tⁿ⁻³ᵏN = N.

The section assumes even positive circumference n and positive k. A necklace has 2k distinct stones, each with signed vector −2, −1, 1 or 2. Consecutive stones have opposite directions. Away-facing gaps are odd; toward-facing gaps plus both vector lengths are odd. A toward-facing gap is at least three, and at gap three both vectors have length one. Necklaces are identified under circle isometries. T performs simultaneous JUMP, then TURN (−2→1, −1→2, 1→−2, 2→−1), then FIX of facing gaps three by shortening length-two vectors to one. Issue #11582 fixes this reading before the probe.
